Why the Entire Market Is Now a Single Bet on AI | The Weekly Wrap

Eisman argues that AI now dominates both incremental US growth and market exposure, making traditional diversification less reliable. He traces how his AI thesis changed as capital spending, model competition and customer pricing became more concerning, using his evolving subprime research as an analogy. He discloses stocks, cash and shorts as his portfolio framework.

How he reasons here

  • Theses develop through accumulating evidence rather than sudden certainty.
  • Look through index and asset-class labels to common economic exposures.
  • Demand durable moats and realized capital returns from large investment budgets.
  • Use historical analogies to search for unrecognized risks, not merely headline opinions.
